You'll partner directly with hiring managers and founders to define role scope, build interview loops, and calibrate what "great" looks like for each role. You: Have run full-cycle recruiting at an early-stage or fast-growing company and know how to own searches end to end. You've worked sales and marketing roles and know how to flex your pitch and interview process for each. You write outbound that gets responses from people who aren't looking, and you know how to close a candidate who has three other offers. You work well solo but you're just as sharp coordinating with other recruiters on shared priorities, and you move fast because slow hiring kills momentum at a company this stage.

jobs.title: Design Engineer
jobs.description_text: Job: We’re hiring a design engineer to help shape and build interactive experiences across Parallel’s website, product, and special projects. The work ranges from refining everyday interactions and motion to creating visual essays, data visualizations, launch pages, and minisites. You’ll work alongside designers, marketers, and engineers from the first rough idea through to production. That means prototyping possible directions, contributing to our core website, and getting the details right in the browser. You’ll also build reusable components and patterns that help us ship the next project faster. You: You’re a design engineer or a frontend engineer with strong design instincts. Your work shows care for typography, layout, and the timing and feel of an interaction. You’ve shipped working websites and can point to the decisions you made along the way. You’re comfortable with modern frontend and animation libraries, and know when to build something custom. You move quickly in prototypes and carry that work through to a responsive, accessible, performant site. About Parallel Design: We design for a web used by both people and agents, grounding our work in real code, data, and evidence. We draw from the history of the web, computing, and publishing to help explain what comes next, while leaving room for experiments, tangents, and things made simply because they’re good.

You'll partner with engineering and marketing to build customer-facing technical content that helps buyers evaluate Parallel, and with Deployed Engineering to turn what they learn in individual deals into scalable resources for the broader team. You’ll spend roughly 80% of your time building and enabling and 20% staying close to live deals to keep everything you build grounded in real customer conversations and challenges. You: You've been a Deployed Engineer, Sales Engineer, or Solutions Engineer for a highly technical product and/or have a strong engineering background. You have 2-3+ years in tech, ideally at a fast-moving startup, and you're fluent with modern AI tools because you use them constantly in your own work. You can write code, quickly understand a customer’s technical challenges, and make complex products clear enough that anyone can pick them up and run with them. Beyond technical fluency, you understand how great sales teams operate and have strong instincts for what helps them win. Product or technical enablement experience is a bonus, not a requirement.

You'll keep Ashby accurate in real time and be the main contact for candidates from first screen to signed offer. You'll work with both the technical and non-technical recruiting teams, handle onboarding logistics with People, and track recruiting metrics so hiring managers and leadership always know where things stand. You'll be Parallel's first coordinator, so you'll design how coordination works here, not inherit it. You: You've coordinated high-volume hiring at a fast-moving company, ideally across both technical and non-technical roles. You know a technical loop runs differently from a sales loop. You've kept an ATS clean when no one was checking. You've rescheduled a five-person panel on short notice without the candidate noticing anything went wrong. You treat every scheduling email as part of the candidate experience, and you handle comp and offer details with discretion. You'd rather build the system once than solve the same problem twice. You flag problems before anyone asks.

jobs.description_text: Agora gave us a pretrained 8B model. Post-training is how we make it useful for agentic use-cases. But every post-training stack you've seen assumes a datacenter — synchronous rollouts, fast interconnects, trusted workers. Ours gets none of that. It has to run on consumer GPUs, and Macs spread across the public internet, training a model whose weights no single participant ever holds, with rollouts arriving from a geo-distributed inference pipeline at high latencies. Your primary role is to make RL post-training work here anyway — the algorithms and the system, end-to-end. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES - Build the post-training stack: You build the RL training loop end-to-end: rollout ingestion from the geo-distributed inference pipeline, reward computation, policy updates, and getting updated weights back out to the network. You set the direction, and you make things happen. - Invent the algorithms: Standard RL recipes assume on-policy rollouts from fast, trusted hardware. You adapt them to asynchronous, high-latency, partially trusted generation: staleness tolerance, off-policy corrections, and communication-efficient policy updates. - Ship first post-trained models: You build the evals that show the models are improving, and you take the first decentralized post-trained release from run to public artifact. jobs.title: Research Engineer - Geo-Distributed Inference

The hardware is Macs and consumer GPUs owned by strangers, the network is the public internet, nodes join and leave mid-run, and the weights change under the server as training moves. jobs.title: Research Engineer - Decentralized Training and Inference Verification
jobs.description_text: Our training and inference network is trustless, and the workers are GPUs scattered across the world. Many things can go wrong in this system. An inference worker can return tokens from a cheaper model, or a highly quantized version of the one it's supposed to run. Even with the right model, it can sample with the wrong parameters. Training faces its own attacks, and Agora showed what a permissionless run deals with in practice: participants who disrupt training by dropping updates or flooding the system, free-riders who submit trivial work and collect the rewards, poisoned updates that plant backdoors, attempts to extract private data from gradients and activations, and contributors who inflate their reported work to claim rewards they didn't earn. Sentinel https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03592 is our first published answer on the training side. Your primary role is to come up with efficient algorithms and systems that verify the work: that tokens came from the claimed model and sampling parameters, and that training contributions are what they claim to be. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES - Own the threat model: You enumerate what a malicious or careless worker can do across pre-training, post-training, and inference — training disruption and denial-of-service, free-riding, model poisoning and backdoors, data extraction from gradients and activations, reputation and reward manipulation — and you keep that model current as the network grows. - Design and calibrate the tests: You build statis

Builder tools are the velocity engine of our platform. This role makes the engine compound: a component built once for one application becomes a primitive available to every application after it. Third, drive the builder tools themselves: the roadmap for Workflow Factory and its sibling builders, and the runtime underneath them, including registries, config-driven backends, and the path from a built workflow to production. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE TEAM The Safety Training research team aims to fundamentally advance our capabilities for precisely implementing safe behavior in AI models, and to leverage these advances to make OpenAI’s deployed models safe and beneficial. This requires a breadth of new ML research to address the growing set of safety challenges as AI becomes more powerful and used in more settings. Key focus areas include how to train nuanced safety behaviors, how to make the model robust to bad actors, how to address privacy and security risks, and how to make the model trustworthy in safety-critical situations. We seek to learn from deployment and distribute the benefits of AI, while ensuring that this powerful tool is used responsibly and safely. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re seeking a researcher to train and evaluate models for U.S. government use, with a focus on national security applications. You’ll advance safety post-training and robustness, helping models follow nuanced policies while preserving their usefulness and capabilities. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Research and implement methods for safety training, reinforcement learning, and adversarial robustness. - Develop evaluations, identify model failure modes, and use findings to improve training. - Work with research, engineering, security, and policy partners to support safe, reliable deployment.
